notice: RN bank batch 132: Mental health case studies: intimate partner violence, elder abuse, postpartum psychosis and sexual assault. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest intimate partner violence.

cells: Answers for the client, will not leave

rationale.correct: Injuries that do not fit the story, controlling behavior and strangulation marks suggest IPV.

perOption.r3: Strangulation, a strong predictor of homicide.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of intimate partner violence.

questions.stem: For each statement, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate about intimate partner violence.

rows.text: Violence often starts or worsens during pregnancy
Prior strangulation greatly raises the risk of homicide
Leaving the relationship is the most dangerous time
A client who stays is choosing the abuse
Abuse follows a cycle of tension, violence and reconciliation

rationale.correct: Pregnancy, strangulation and separation raise danger.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first step is to {{b1}}, then {{b2}}.

options.text: interview the client alone, away from the partner
ask the partner what happened
confront the partner about the injuries
call the police immediately without telling the client
ask directly and privately about safety at home
tell the client to leave the partner today
document only the fall
discharge quickly

rationale.correct: Separate, then ask directly.

perOption.b1:d: Adult IPV reporting depends on state law and the client's wishes.
perOption.b2:b: The client decides; leaving can be dangerous.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The client discloses abuse but says, "I can't leave. I have nowhere to go." Which actions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Build a safety plan with the client
Give hotline and shelter information in a safe form
Document injuries with a body map, photos with consent and the client's own words
Complete a lethality assessment
Insist that the client go to a shelter tonight
Give printed pamphlets the partner might find

rationale.correct: Safety plan, discreet resources, accurate documentation and lethality assessment.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Private interview
exhibits.body: The client says the partner choked them last month and owns a gun.

questions.stem: The partner demands to see the chart and asks what the client told staff. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Decline to share any information without the client's consent
Call security if the partner becomes threatening
Mark the client's record so information is not given by phone
Tell the partner what the client disclosed to calm things down
Discharge the client with the partner to avoid conflict

rationale.correct: Protect confidentiality and safety.

questions.stem: Before discharge, for each statement, indicate whether it shows a safer plan or needs follow-up.

rows.text: "I memorized the hotline number and deleted it from my phone."

"I'll keep my prenatal appointments where I can talk alone."

questions.stem: The son says, "I know I've lost my temper. I'm so tired." Which responses are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Caring for her every night is exhausting."
"What happens when you lose your temper?"
"You should be ashamed of yourself for treating your mother like this."
"Don't worry, everyone does that sometimes."
"I won't tell anyone about this, it can stay between us."

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it fits postpartum blues, postpartum depression or postpartum psychosis.

rows.text: Tearful days 3 to 5, resolves within 2 weeks
Low mood for weeks with guilt and poor bonding
Hallucinations and confusion in the first 2 weeks
Intrusive fear of harming the baby that horrifies the mother
Belief that harming the baby is the right thing

rationale.correct: Timing, duration and psychosis separate the three.

perOption.r4:c2: Ego-dystonic thoughts in depression or OCD.
perOption.r4:c3: Ego-dystonic thoughts in depression or OCD.

questions.stem: Which actions protect the evidence and the client? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ask the client not to drink, eat, wash or urinate until samples are taken, if possible
Collect clothing in paper bags
Keep the chain of custody
Draw blood and urine for toxicology with consent
Store the clothing in a sealed plastic bag
Leave the evidence kit at the desk while the nurse takes a break

caseStudies.title: Elder abuse and neglect of a client with dementia

exhibits.title: Home visit
exhibits.body: An 84-year-old client with moderate Alzheimer disease lives with a son who is the only caregiver and lost his job recently. The son says, "I can't do this anymore. She wanders all night." The client's pension is paid into the son's account.

rows.label: Wrists
cells: Bruises in a band pattern on both wrists

rows.label: Medicines
cells: Donepezil bottle full; filled 2 months ago

rows.label: Client
cells: Flinches when the son raises his voice

exhibits.title: Day 6 after birth
exhibits.body: A 26-year-old client with a history of bipolar disorder (stopped lithium in pregnancy) gave birth 6 days ago. The partner calls: the client has not slept for 3 nights, is talking fast, and says the baby "has the devil in him and needs to be saved."

rows.label: Perceptions
cells: Hears God telling her to save the baby

rows.label: Baby
cells: At home with the client and partner

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 20-year-old client arrives with a friend 6 hours after being sexually assaulted by an acquaintance at a party. The client says, "I think something was put in my drink. I can't remember most of it." The client is shaking and calm by turns.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
